back: Correspondence: 25 or fewer retail investors in 30 days. More: retail communication.
spoken: Twenty-five or fewer retail investors in thirty days is correspondence. More is a retail communication.

back: Registered Options Principal, before use (Rule 2220).
spoken: Options retail communications need a registered options principal's approval before use.

back: At least 20 days. Red herring and indications of interest allowed; no sales or payments.
spoken: Cooling off lasts at least twenty days. You can hand out the red herring and take indications of interest, but no sales.

back: Income > $200K ($300K joint) in each of last 2 years, or net worth > $1M excluding primary residence.
spoken: Accredited individual: over two hundred thousand of income for two years, three hundred joint, or over a million in net worth without the home.

back: $250 per election, only to officials the MFP can vote for.
spoken: G thirty-seven allows two hundred fifty dollars per election, only to officials you can vote for.

back: Any written communication distributed or made available to more than 25 retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period.
spoken: Retail communication. Any written communication distributed or made available to more than twenty-five retail investors within any thirty-calendar-day period.

back: Any written communication distributed to 25 or fewer retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period.
spoken: Correspondence. Any written communication distributed to twenty-five or fewer retail investors within any thirty-calendar-day period.

back: A written communication distributed only to institutional investors, which needs supervisory procedures but not prior principal approval.
spoken: Institutional communication. A written communication distributed only to institutional investors, which needs supervisory procedures but not prior principal approval.

back: Under FINRA's communications rule, any person other than an institutional investor, whether or not the person has an account.
spoken: Retail investor. Under FINRA's communications rule, any person other than an institutional investor, whether or not the person has an account.

back: Participation in a seminar, webinar, forum, interview or other public speaking activity, which is not itself a written communication.
spoken: Public appearance. Participation in a seminar, webinar, forum, interview or other public speaking activity, which is not itself a written communication.

back: A statement by a customer or other person about their experience with a firm or representative, which must disclose if more than 100 dollars was paid for it.
spoken: Testimonial. A statement by a customer or other person about their experience with a firm or representative, which must disclose if more than one hundred dollars was paid for it.

back: A requirement that a new firm file retail communications with FINRA at least 10 business days before first use during its first year.
spoken: New member filing requirement. A requirement that a new firm file retail communications with FINRA at least ten business days before first use during its first year.

back: An article issued by an unaffiliated publisher that a firm redistributes, which is treated as a retail communication.
spoken: Independently prepared reprint. An article issued by an unaffiliated publisher that a firm redistributes, which is treated as a retail communication.

back: The OCC booklet called Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options, delivered at or before options account approval.
spoken: Options Disclosure Document. The OCC booklet called Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options, delivered at or before options account approval.

back: A short-form open-end fund prospectus with key facts, permitted under SEC Rule 498, with the full prospectus available on request.
spoken: Summary prospectus. A short-form open-end fund prospectus with key facts, permitted under SEC Rule four hundred ninety-eight, with the full prospectus available on request.

back: An investment company ad that may contain information not in the prospectus, but must urge investors to read the prospectus and show standardized performance if performance appears.
spoken: Rule four hundred eighty-two advertisement. An investment company ad that may contain information not in the prospectus, but must urge investors to read the prospectus and show standardized performance if performance appears.

back: The SEC rule that bars investment company sales literature from being materially misleading.
spoken: SEC Rule one hundred fifty-six. The SEC rule that bars investment company sales literature from being materially misleading.

back: A period around an offering during which the underwriters' research reports and research analysts' public appearances are restricted.
spoken: Quiet period. A period around an offering during which the underwriters' research reports and research analysts' public appearances are restricted.

back: A description of a bond fund's sensitivity to changing market conditions, permitted in communications only under specific FINRA conditions.
spoken: Bond fund volatility rating. A description of a bond fund's sensitivity to changing market conditions, permitted in communications only under specific FINRA conditions.

back: The FINRA requirement that CMO communications use the term collateralized mortgage obligation and never compare CMOs to any other investment, such as CDs.
spoken: CMO communication rule. The FINRA requirement that CMO communications use the term collateralized mortgage obligation and never compare CMOs to any other investment, such as CDs.

back: A comparison of a fund's performance to peers that, in retail communications, must come from an independent ranking entity.
spoken: Investment company ranking. A comparison of a fund's performance to peers that, in retail communications, must come from an independent ranking entity.

back: The disclosure document an issuer files with the SEC under the Securities Act of 1933 before a public offering.
spoken: Registration statement. The disclosure document an issuer files with the SEC under the Securities Act of one thousand nine hundred thirty-three before a public offering.

back: The period of at least 20 days between filing a registration statement and its effective date, when no sales may be made.
spoken: Cooling-off period. The period of at least twenty days between filing a registration statement and its effective date, when no sales may be made.

back: The preliminary prospectus, which omits the final offering price and carries a legend that the registration is not yet effective.
spoken: Red herring. The preliminary prospectus, which omits the final offering price and carries a legend that the registration is not yet effective.

back: The offering document that includes the public offering price and must be delivered no later than confirmation of the sale.
spoken: Final prospectus. The offering document that includes the public offering price and must be delivered no later than confirmation of the sale.

back: The meeting during the cooling-off period where underwriters review the issuer's disclosures to establish a reasonable basis for the offering.
spoken: Due diligence meeting. The meeting during the cooling-off period where underwriters review the issuer's disclosures to establish a reasonable basis for the offering.

back: State securities laws that require offerings to be registered or qualified in each state where they are sold.
spoken: Blue-sky laws. State securities laws that require offerings to be registered or qualified in each state where they are sold.

back: An underwriting in which the syndicate buys the whole issue from the issuer and bears the risk of unsold shares.
spoken: Firm commitment underwriting. An underwriting in which the syndicate buys the whole issue from the issuer and bears the risk of unsold shares.

back: An underwriting in which the underwriter acts as agent and returns any unsold securities to the issuer.
spoken: Best efforts underwriting. An underwriting in which the underwriter acts as agent and returns any unsold securities to the issuer.

back: A best efforts underwriting that is canceled and funds returned if the entire issue is not sold.
spoken: All-or-none underwriting. A best efforts underwriting that is canceled and funds returned if the entire issue is not sold.

back: An agreement to buy any shares left unsubscribed at the end of a rights offering.
spoken: Standby underwriting. An agreement to buy any shares left unsubscribed at the end of a rights offering.

back: A bid entered by the managing underwriter at or below the public offering price to support an issue's price in the aftermarket.
spoken: Stabilizing bid. A bid entered by the managing underwriter at or below the public offering price to support an issue's price in the aftermarket.

back: A simple announcement of an offering listing the issuer, the security, the price and where a prospectus can be obtained.
spoken: Tombstone ad. A simple announcement of an offering listing the issuer, the security, the price and where a prospectus can be obtained.

back: The SEC rules that restrict underwriters and issuers from bidding for or buying the offered security during a distribution, with exceptions such as stabilization.
spoken: Regulation M. The SEC rules that restrict underwriters and issuers from bidding for or buying the offered security during a distribution, with exceptions such as stabilization.

back: A written offer that is not a statutory prospectus, permitted after the registration statement is filed under conditions in SEC rules.
spoken: Free writing prospectus. A written offer that is not a statutory prospectus, permitted after the registration statement is filed under conditions in SEC rules.

back: The Regulation D private placement exemption that bars general solicitation and allows up to 35 non-accredited but sophisticated purchasers.
spoken: Rule five hundred six(b). The Regulation D private placement exemption that bars general solicitation and allows up to thirty-five non-accredited but sophisticated purchasers.

back: The Regulation D exemption that permits general solicitation if every purchaser is accredited and the issuer takes reasonable steps to verify it.
spoken: Rule five hundred six(c). The Regulation D exemption that permits general solicitation if every purchaser is accredited and the issuer takes reasonable steps to verify it.

back: A small-issue exemption that uses an offering circular and has two tiers, with Tier 2 allowing up to 75 million dollars in 12 months.
spoken: Regulation A. A small-issue exemption that uses an offering circular and has two tiers, with Tier two allowing up to seventy-five million dollars in twelve months.

back: An intrastate offering exemption requiring the issuer and all purchasers to be in one state, with resales to nonresidents limited for six months.
spoken: Rule one hundred forty-seven. An intrastate offering exemption requiring the issuer and all purchasers to be in one state, with resales to nonresidents limited for six months.

back: The SEC rule governing public resales of restricted and control securities, including holding periods and volume limits.
spoken: Rule one hundred forty-four. The SEC rule governing public resales of restricted and control securities, including holding periods and volume limits.

back: The exemption that allows resales of unregistered securities to qualified institutional buyers.
spoken: Rule 144A. The exemption that allows resales of unregistered securities to qualified institutional buyers.

back: An institution that owns and invests at least 100 million dollars in securities of unaffiliated issuers, eligible to buy under Rule 144A.
spoken: Qualified institutional buyer. An institution that owns and invests at least one hundred million dollars in securities of unaffiliated issuers, eligible to buy under Rule 144A.

back: The exemption for offers and sales made outside the United States without SEC registration.
spoken: Regulation S. The exemption for offers and sales made outside the United States without SEC registration.

back: Securities held by an officer, director or 10 percent or more shareholder of the issuer, which must be sold under Rule 144 limits.
spoken: Control securities. Securities held by an officer, director or ten percent or more shareholder of the issuer, which must be sold under Rule one hundred forty-four limits.

back: Securities acquired in an unregistered private transaction that cannot be resold publicly until a holding period is met.
spoken: Restricted securities. Securities acquired in an unregistered private transaction that cannot be resold publicly until a holding period is met.

back: A security that is not required to register with the SEC, such as a U.S. government or municipal bond.
spoken: Exempt security. A security that is not required to register with the SEC, such as a U.S. government or municipal bond.

back: The exemption that lets small issuers raise limited amounts online through a registered funding portal or broker-dealer.
spoken: Regulation Crowdfunding. The exemption that lets small issuers raise limited amounts online through a registered funding portal or broker-dealer.

back: The issuer's published invitation for bids in a competitive municipal sale, stating the terms and the bid deadline.
spoken: Notice of sale. The issuer's published invitation for bids in a competitive municipal sale, stating the terms and the bid deadline.

back: The municipal offering document prepared by the issuer that discloses the terms and risks of a new issue.
spoken: Official statement. The municipal offering document prepared by the issuer that discloses the terms and risks of a new issue.

back: The draft municipal offering document used before final pricing to gauge interest.
spoken: Preliminary official statement. The draft municipal offering document used before final pricing to gauge interest.

back: A syndicate account in which each member is liable only for its own allocation of bonds.
spoken: Western account. A syndicate account in which each member is liable only for its own allocation of bonds.

back: A syndicate account in which each member is liable for its share of any bonds left unsold by the whole syndicate.
spoken: Eastern account. A syndicate account in which each member is liable for its share of any bonds left unsold by the whole syndicate.

back: The discount at which a syndicate member buys bonds from the syndicate, equal to the total spread minus the manager's fee.
spoken: Takedown. The discount at which a syndicate member buys bonds from the syndicate, equal to the total spread minus the manager's fee.

back: The portion of the spread a selling group member earns on bonds it sells.
spoken: Concession. The portion of the spread a selling group member earns on bonds it sells.

back: The portion of the takedown kept by a syndicate member, over and above the concession.
spoken: Additional takedown. The portion of the takedown kept by a syndicate member, over and above the concession.

back: The portion of the underwriting spread paid to the managing underwriter for organizing the syndicate.
spoken: Manager's fee. The portion of the underwriting spread paid to the managing underwriter for organizing the syndicate.

back: A municipal order credited to all syndicate members according to their participation, typically given top priority.
spoken: Group net order. A municipal order credited to all syndicate members according to their participation, typically given top priority.

back: A municipal order, usually from an institution, that names which syndicate members receive credit for the sale.
spoken: Designated order. A municipal order, usually from an institution, that names which syndicate members receive credit for the sale.

back: A syndicate member's own order at the takedown price, usually filled last.
spoken: Member order. A syndicate member's own order at the takedown price, usually filled last.

back: A deposit submitted with a competitive bid to show the syndicate will honor its bid.
spoken: Good faith deposit. A deposit submitted with a competitive bid to show the syndicate will honor its bid.

back: Bond counsel's opinion on the legality of an issue and the tax status of its interest.
spoken: Legal opinion. Bond counsel's opinion on the legality of an issue and the tax status of its interest.

back: A legal opinion given without reservations.
spoken: Unqualified opinion. A legal opinion given without reservations.

back: The issuer's ongoing filing of annual financial information and material event notices on EMMA, required through underwriter agreements under SEC Rule 15c2-12.
spoken: Continuing disclosure. The issuer's ongoing filing of annual financial information and material event notices on EMMA, required through underwriter agreements under SEC Rule 15c2-twelve.

back: The pay-to-play rule that limits political contributions by municipal finance professionals and bars municipal business for two years after a covered contribution.
spoken: MSRB Rule G-thirty-seven. The pay-to-play rule that limits political contributions by municipal finance professionals and bars municipal business for two years after a covered contribution.
